config.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor

intro.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that automatically refreshes an expired authentication token using Axios interceptors. You'll learn how to intercept HTTP requests and responses to check for token expiration and handle a refresh request seamlessly. The core concepts involve using Axios interceptors, managing asynchronous API calls, and updating application state with the new token. You'll work with React hooks, TypeScript interfaces for type safety, and a mock authentication service to simulate the token refresh flow.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications like dashboards, admin panels, or e-commerce sites, user sessions must remain active without requiring manual re-login. This pattern is essential when making API calls that require authentication tokens, which often expire. For example, in a financial dashboard, an expired token during a data refresh would disrupt the user's workflow. Implementing an Axios interceptor to automatically refresh tokens ensures seamless, uninterrupted user experiences by handling token expiration silently in the background.

objectives: Initialize an Axios instance with a base configuration for API requests
Configure an Axios request interceptor to attach authentication tokens to outgoing requests
Implement an Axios response interceptor to detect expired token responses
Construct a token refresh mechanism that makes a new authentication request
Integrate the token refresh logic with the response interceptor to retry failed requests
Apply error handling to manage failed token refresh attempts
Update the Axios instance configuration to use the new token for subsequent requests

steps.instruction: Inside your App component, add a request interceptor to your axios instance that injects the access token into the Authorization header of outgoing requests.
steps.hint: Use the axios instance's interceptors.request.use() method. The interceptor function should modify the config object to add headers.Authorization with the token value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The axios instance will automatically attach the authorization header to all requests made through it.
successCriteria: A request interceptor is added using interceptors.request.use() that sets the Authorization header with a token value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an interceptor, but make sure it correctly sets the Authorization header on the config object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request interceptor is missing or incorrectly implemented. Use interceptors.request.use() to modify the config headers.

steps.hint: Use axiosInstance.interceptors.response.use() to add the interceptor. The first argument should handle successful responses, the second should handle errors.
